newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour advances strongly in latest poll.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour advances strongly in latest poll.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party extended its lead over the ruling Conservatives to 27 points from 25 points in the past week, according to an opinion poll for Friday's Independent newspaper.
But the Harris poll also said most voters still believed that Prime Minister John Major's Conservative Party could win the May 1 general election.

While 56 percent of those questioned said they would vote Labour to 29 percent for the Conservatives, 52 percent agreed that Major's party could win an unprecedented fifth term of office. Only 20 percent said they were convinced that Labour would win.
Other surveys published in the past week have given Labour leads of 25 and 28 points, but Labour leader Tony Blair said in an interview that opinion polls could not be relied on.
"I think it is going to be a far tighter and harder race than (polls) suggest," he said.

The Harris poll has shown a steady widening of Labour's lead over the past month. On March 14, it put support for Labour at 52 percent and the Conservatives at 27 percent. A week earlier, Labour was at 53 percent and the Conservatives at 32 percent.
The poll also said Labour voters were more likely to turn out on polling day, with 69 percent saying they were "certain" to vote against 60 percent of Conservative supporters.
Harris interviewed 1,016 potential voters between March 14 and 17.
